_comment: Hunt patterns shipped with SHELLHOUND. Read-only: this file lives in the
package, not in the workspace, so an upgrade brings new entries and the
analyst's own library is never touched. An entry can be switched off per
workspace; it cannot be edited, because editing it while it keeps its id
and its CVE would make the same identifier mean different things on two
AN ENTRY IS: one or more paths, a name, the advisory it belongs to, and
what a hit proves. `match` says how several paths combine -- OVER CLIENTS,
not over one request: 'any' is a client that hit at least one of them,
'all' only clients that hit every one.
WHAT A HIT PROVES: that a request was made. Nothing here says the request
succeeded, and nothing here is a finding on its own -- the status code
decides, and that is what the hunt reports back.
THE SET IS DELIBERATELY SHORT. A pattern that ships is one every
installation runs, so a false positive here does not cost one analyst a
look -- it costs all of them a filled work list.
ids are stable strings, never regenerated: the per-workspace off-switch
refers to them across versions. '*' is a wildcard, not a regex.

patterns.name: Joomla JCE editor RCE
patterns.description: CVE-2026-48907 is a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting the Joomla Content Editor (JCE) extension. Due to improper access control, unauthenticated attackers can upload and execute malicious PHP files, potentially leading to full compromise of the affected web server.

patterns.name: Joomla Helix3 unauthenticated ajax handler
patterns.description: The Helix3 template framework registers an ajax handler that Joomla routes to without checking a session. A request that names it reached that handler. WHAT A HIT DOES NOT PROVE: that the call succeeded. com_ajax answers 200 with a JSON body whether the handler accepted the input or rejected it, so the status code settles nothing here and a hit on its own is a lead rather than a finding. Corroborate against the Helix3 version in the CMS inventory, a file in the webroot whose .php is not its last extension, or template settings that changed. ONE TOKEN, DELIBERATELY. Matching `helix3` alone selects the template's static assets -- measured on a real site that has it installed: 11,183 clients, i.e. every visitor. `plugin=helix3` selects 3. Adding `option=com_ajax` as a second path buys nothing, because `plugin=helix3` appears nowhere else, and costs robustness against reordered query strings.

patterns.name: wp2shell PoC plugin webshell
patterns.description: The requested URI matches the random wp-content/plugins/wp2shell_<suffix>/wp2shell_<suffix>.php endpoint created and invoked by public wp2shell proof-of-concept tools. This is a high-signal, PoC-specific trace that the deployed plugin shell was addressed. WHAT A HIT DOES NOT PROVE: the access log does not contain the nested batch JSON body and therefore cannot prove that REST route confusion or SQL injection succeeded; an operator can also rename the plugin or drop a shell elsewhere. Corroborate with POST requests to /wp-json/batch/v1 or ?rest_route=/batch/v1, HTTP 207 responses, /wp-admin/update.php?action=upload-plugin, an unexpected administrator account, and the corresponding PHP artifact in the webroot.
